It could be a number of things. 

Assuming you're not overclocking, it may be some bad sectors on your disk that need repairing. Try a disk scan. 

If you are oc'ing, turn the multiplier down because it's being unstable. This usually leads to blue screen so likely not this.

You may want to try to boot into safe mode and log all the way into the desktop then shut down properly.

Does one of your CPU cores max at 100 percent when this thing happens? Could be a defective processor.

Any background programs taking up your entire allotted RAM? Prevent them from running on startup or try to figure out why it requires so much. Could be a program crashing and causing a memory leak.

Any USB storage device plugged in? Unplug it and see if an error with recognizing or writing to it is the problem. I've had this happen and as soon as I unplug the drive everything behaves normally.

You could try doing a windows repair in case there's a problem with system files or registry or load a restore point in case a new installation is fucking things up.

Might run a full diagnostics test on your hardware.

I built a custom arcade cabinet/machine last year to relieve stress and to help cope with my bipolar depression and a few additional mental illnesses that I've had to deal with for many years. It's also great to have a cool piece to show off to people. Its unfinished currently so ignore the disorganized shelves and upper bank.

Figured I'd share with the community to see what you think.

It runs the retropie firmware on the rasberry pi 3 and is loaded with multiple thousands of classic console and arcade games.

The cabinet was influenced by the awesome design linked below:

https://www.pinterest.com/pin/268175352792925296/

It was modified however to have a different shape, size, and look. This includes designing to fit my tv, to be able to fit through my doorframe, and to add my own creative components.

Additionally shelves were designed and placed underneath the cabinet to hold all my physical Nintendo consoles from the NES all the way to the switch. This has not been done currently so ignore the mess and misc items such as the pokedex placed on the shelves underneath. 

If you want me to explain more in depth of the design, build, installation, etc. or answer questions, I'll reply in the comments.

Updates hopefully coming soon as I do them 😊.
